teams.heading: Interim coach Senirusi Seruvakula seeks improvement with Fiji bottom of the table
teams.body: Fiji occupies 12th place in the Nations Championship standings after three matches, following a 17-33 defeat to Scotland in the previous round. Under interim head coach Senirusi Seruvakula, the side has registered 49 points and conceded 145 across the tournament so far, leaving them with a points difference of -96. While the Flying Fijians reached a record world ranking of No. 7 in 2023, the squad is currently the only winless side in the competition.

teams.heading: England women hire Shaun Edwards as defence consultant for WXV series
teams.body: England women have secured the services of legendary defence guru Shaun Edwards in a consultancy role for the remainder of the WXV Global Series. The Red Roses move follows Edwards' departure from the France men’s setup in June, with head coach John Mitchell describing his credentials as “exceptional” at the highest level. Edwards will work alongside Sarah Hunter ahead of Saturday’s test against New Zealand. It marks the first time the former Wales coach has worked within the women’s international game.

teams.heading: Jean-Marc Lhermet defends France's leaked elite player list following public uproar
teams.body: A leaked resource-sharing agreement between the FFR and LNR has caused friction across the Top 14 after Midi-Olympique published a secret list of 33 "premium" players. The deal restricts these individuals to nine internationals per season and mandates regular rest periods to prioritise the national side. FFR vice-president Jean-Marc Lhermet was forced to justify the metrics after fans questioned the absence of Grégory Alldritt and Maxime Lucu. Toulouse are set to be the hardest hit, with 13 players reportedly included on the protected roster.

teams.heading: Scott Bemand rues massive collapse as Ireland women surrender 19-point lead
teams.body: Ireland women’s head coach Scott Bemand admitted his side "should have won" Sunday’s WXV opener after surrendering a 19-point lead against the USA. Despite scoring six tries at Tallaght Stadium, the hosts collapsed during the final quarter as the Eagles scored four unanswered tries to overturn a 31-12 deficit. Bemand criticised a second-half loss of discipline and technical control that allowed the visitors to snatch a 40-36 victory. Ireland must now regroup before facing Japan in Galway to keep their WXV campaign alive.

teams.heading: Italy Women crush Japan Women as Vittoria Ostuni Minuzzi earns 50th cap
teams.body: Italy Women secured their largest-ever victory over Japan Women with a dominant 55-21 win to open their WXV Global Series campaign. After an early scare saw the Sakura XV take a brief lead, the Azzurre responded with five first-half tries, including clinical efforts from Alyssa D'Inca and Vittoria Vecchini. The Italy captain marked her 50th cap with a second-half score as the Italians outplayed their opponents in all facets at Stadio Omero Tognon.

teams.heading: Scotland Women await official Sky Sports confirmation for inaugural 2027 Lions tour
teams.body: Scotland Women are still awaiting official confirmation that Sky Sports has secured the broadcast rights for the inaugural 2027 British & Irish Lions tour. Despite reports last week that an agreement was imminent, the Lions board has offered no further update today. The deal is crucial for the visibility of the New Zealand series, which remains a key target for the national squad following Saturday’s 14-66 WXV defeat by the Black Ferns. The Scots, featuring two-try scorer Evie Gallagher, now refocus for Australia this weekend.

teams.heading: Dewi Lake named Gloucester captain with Jac Morgan serving as deputy
teams.body: Wales hooker Dewi Lake has been appointed Gloucester captain for the 2026/27 season, with fellow Welsh international Jac Morgan named among the club’s vice-captains. The duo, who previously led Wales as co-captains during the 2023 World Cup, have reunited at Kingsholm following their departure from the Ospreys. Gloucester head coach George Skivington confirmed the decision followed input from the playing group, noting that “Dewi’s leadership experience is there for everyone to see” ahead of their upcoming league campaign.

teams.heading: Argentina men and women celebrate historic double gold in Rosario games
teams.body: Argentina’s rugby sevens programmes cemented their status as the continent's premier force by securing a golden double at the Juegos Suramericanos in Rosario. The men’s team claimed victory with a 17–7 result over Chile, while Las Yaguaretés ended Brazil’s decade-long dominance with a 35–5 win against Colombia. These clinical performances ensure both sides have officially locked in their automatic qualification for the 2027 Pan American Games, maintaining the country's momentum on the international stage.

teams.heading: Andre Esterhuizen named captain as Springboks make 13 changes for Australia
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has rung the changes for Sunday’s Test in Perth, handing Andre Esterhuizen the captaincy in an overhauled Springbok starting XV. The centre leads a side featuring 13 alterations from the team that recently finished their series against the All Blacks. Only lock Eben Etzebeth and winger Ethan Hooker retain their spots. Australia’s forwards coach Tom Donnelly admits the hosts face a physical test, noting, “We know what’s coming” as they look to build on their improving set-piece performance.

teams.heading: Japan Brave Blossoms claim Pacific Nations Cup title against resilient Fiji
teams.body: The Brave Blossoms secured their first Pacific Nations Cup title since 2019, overcoming Fiji 20-15 in a physical encounter at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium. The win, which coincides with the 11th anniversary of their famous 2015 victory over South Africa, lifts Japan into the world’s top ten rankings. Captain Naoto Saito hailed the result as a pivotal breakthrough, stating, “This is going to be the trigger for us to break through and create new history for Japan.”

lead.why: Japan securing the Pacific Nations Cup title is the most significant recent development for the men's national side.

teams.heading: Captain Ardie Savea ruled out with injury as long-term list grows
teams.body: All Blacks skipper Ardie Savea faces a lengthy period on the sidelines following confirmation that he requires surgery on a dislocated shoulder sustained during the recent Test series against the Springboks. The loss of Savea is compounded by a significant injury toll, with fellow loose forward Luke Jacobson and winger Caleb Clarke both ruled out for several months. Further recovery timelines for Anton Lienert-Brown, Quinn Tupaea, Anton Segner, Cortez Ratima, and Billy Proctor leave the squad managing a considerable end-of-season toll.

teams.heading: André Esterhuizen named Springboks captain for refreshed side against Wallabies
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has appointed André Esterhuizen to lead a significantly rotated South Africa side against Australia in Perth this weekend. The 32-year-old will become the 68th player to captain the Springboks, earning the honour after making 13 changes to the starting XV that defeated New Zealand. "He captained the Hollywoodbets Sharks, and he has brought so much to our squad off and on the field, both at centre and in the loose trio, and he thoroughly deserves this opportunity," Erasmus stated.
